title: Run docket grid — personal tracker
content:
Purpose: quick personal mini-sheet to keep a compact, per-session ledger of micro-bench runs. Not production, mostly scratch + immediate observations.

Layout: one-line rows keyed by run_id, then quick notes. Use this when doing on-the-fly probes from my laptop or a small debug instance.

Table (columns): date | run_id | model | variant | hw | batch | seq | quant | p50_ms | p95_ms | cost_per_1k_tokens | cache_hit_pct | notes

2026-02-02 | R-2602-a | redwood-v2-7B | fp16 | gtx-a500 | 8 | 128 | f16 | 12 | 34 | $0.18 | 0% | baseline, cold start; weird p95 bump at 6s mark
2026-02-03 | R-2603-b | redwood-v2-7B | int8 | gtx-a500 | 8 | 128 | int8 | 10 | 28 | $0.12 | 0% | int8 looks fine, minor quality regression in long-form generation
2026-02-05 | R-2605-c | redwood-v2-7B | int8-cached | gtx-a500 | 8 | 128 | int8 | 6 | 16 | $0.09 | 48% | prefix cache hit helps p50; maintain for small seqs
2026-02-10 | R-2610-d | redwood-v2-7B | int8-batched | gtx-a500 | 16 | 128 | int8 | 8 | 22 | $0.07 | 0% | increased throughput; latency per-request up slightly vs cached
2026-02-12 | R-2612-e | redwood-v2-13B | fp16 | rtx-6000 | 8 | 256 | f16 | 28 | 72 | $0.45 | 0% | larger model, expected; p95 sensitive to seq>200
2026-02-15 | R-2615-f | redwood-v2-13B | q4_1 | rtx-6000 | 8 | 256 | q4_1 | 18 | 40 | $0.22 | 0% | q4_1 tradeoff: good latency, check hallucination rate on eval set

Quick obs:
- Pattern: cache+int8 beats cold fp16 for 7B on cost and p50; p95 sometimes unpredictable with occasional GC-like spike.
- Batching helps throughput but not p95 for low-concurrency requests; consider dynamic routing for latency-sensitive routes.
- Sequence length threshold around 200 tokens spikes p95 for 13B — file as regression candidate if prod sees longer prompts.

Notes to self (TODO):
- [ ] Re-run R-2603-b with prompt truncation to confirm quality delta at seq 512.
- [ ] Add a tiny eval harness for top-5 generations to measure semantic drift for int8 variants. Link to GH PR above.
- [ ] Probe memory growth when switching between variants rapidly (possible non-returning alloc).

Scratch thoughts / fringe ideas:
- Consider a tiny rolling-window metric in the console: "ghost spikes per hour" (counts p95 jumps > 2x baseline). Could help correlate with GC, host temp, or cache thrash.
- If cache hit rate >40% and p50 < 8ms, consider autopromote to default for low-cost plan.

Recent quick links and notes:
- Log: /tmp/run-docket-logs/2026-02 (local) — grep for R-26* for raw samples.
- Slack thread (bench-ops): convo id: bench-ops/2026-02-05 "cache warmup anomalies".
- GH PR: bench harness change (see linked_artifacts) includes small metric exporters for p50/p95 and sample outputs.

Questions unresolved:
- Are the p95 spikes correlated with any preemption/backfill events on rtx-6000 instances? Need SRE trace.
- Cache eviction pattern: do small prefixes evict frequently if batch size increases? add a small microtest.

End of run-docket entry. Will keep appending runs here during the day; once a stable pattern emerges move to a formal sheet under /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmarks.
